title: Greek Temples
objective: After this level you can name the three Greek column styles and describe the Parthenon.
summary: Greek columns come in three orders: Doric, Ionic and Corinthian. The Parthenon, built from 447 BCE for Athena, is the peak of Doric, full of subtle curves still debated.

cards.headline: The Parthenon looks perfectly straight. It isn't.
cards.body: Its base bulges upward in the middle and its columns swell slightly. People have argued about why since Roman times. First, though, learn to read a Greek column from the top.

cards.headline: Three column styles, read from the top

items.label: Doric
points: No base; a plain, cushion-like capital

items.label: Ionic
points: Stands on a base; more slender

cards.headline: The Parthenon
cards.body: Built of white marble from 447 BCE and finished by 438 BCE, the Parthenon honored the goddess Athena. Its architects, Ictinus and Callicrates, worked under the sculptor Phidias, and they made it the high point of the simplest order, Doric. Simple, here, doesn't mean plain: almost nothing about this building is as straight as it looks.

cards.fact: The Parthenon's base rises about 5 cm in the middle.
cards.context: Its columns bulge slightly (entasis), and its corner columns are thicker. The classic explanation comes from the Roman architect Vitruvius: the curves correct optical illusions, so the temple looks straight. In 2026, the mathematician Alain Goriely argued there's no evidence the curves produce those illusions at all. The curves are measured fact; the reason is still an argument.

mascot.line: Measure first, explain second. The Parthenon keeps both jobs busy.

cards.headline: Greek temples: read
learned: Doric: plain; Ionic: scrolls; Corinthian: leaves
Its base curves up in the middle
Why the curves exist is still debated

questions.prompt: You spot a column topped with carved acanthus leaves. Which order is it?

options.label: Doric
options.rationale: Doric capitals are plain and cushion-like.

options.label: Ionic
options.rationale: Ionic capitals have scrolls, not leaves.

questions.explanation: Corinthian capitals are carved with rows of acanthus leaves, the most decorative of the three orders.

questions.prompt: What do scholars still disagree about in the Parthenon's curves?

options.label: Whether the curves exist
options.rationale: They're measured: the base rises about 5 cm in the middle.

options.label: Which order its columns follow
options.rationale: It is the high point of the Doric order.

questions.explanation: Vitruvius said the curves correct optical illusions; a 2026 study argues there's no evidence they do. The reason is debated.

questions.prompt: The Parthenon honored Athena. Which god did the ziggurat at Ur serve (Level 11)?

options.label: Apollo, god of the sun and light
options.rationale: Ur's tower was for a Mesopotamian god.

options.label: Ur-Nammu
options.rationale: He was the king who built it.

options.label: Athena as well
options.rationale: Athena was Greek; Ur's god was Mesopotamian.

questions.explanation: Both were homes for a god on high: the Parthenon for Athena, Ur's ziggurat and its summit temple for the moon god Nanna.
